Discussion

1. Review of Sprint 23 outcomes and velocity

  • The team completed 34 of 40 committed story points (85%). Average velocity over the last three sprints is 36 points.
  • Two stories carried over: the notification preferences API (blocked by a pending security review) and the onboarding checklist UI (design revisions arrived late).
  • Sofia noted that two escaped defects in the search filter were found after release; both are fixed and a regression test was added.
  • Retro follow-up: the team agreed that design hand-offs should happen before sprint start, not during the sprint.

2. Sprint 24 goal and priorities

  • Maria proposed the goal: "Ship the redesigned onboarding flow to 25% of new users and complete notification preferences."
  • Leadership wants onboarding conversion data before the end-of-year planning cycle, so the onboarding rollout is the top priority.
  • Marcus provided analytics requirements by message: track step completion and drop-off per step, plus time to first key action.
  • Daniel asked that tech debt work be limited to one small item to protect the goal.

3. Backlog review and story estimation

StoryEstimateNotes
Onboarding flow: steps 1–3 UI8 ptsCarried over; designs now final
Onboarding: feature flag and 25% rollout5 ptsNeeds experiment config from Tom
Onboarding analytics events5 ptsDepends on Marcus's event spec

  • Total committed: 38 points, slightly above the 36-point average. The team agreed this is acceptable because the carried-over stories are partly done.
  • The team debated splitting the onboarding UI story. Aisha preferred to keep it whole to avoid integration overhead, and Daniel agreed.
  • A proposed in-app tooltip tour (13 pts) was too large and too uncertain, so it was moved to the backlog for refinement.

4. Capacity and risks

  • Capacity is reduced by about 10% because Tom is out Dec 3–4 and the US Thanksgiving holiday falls on Nov 26–27 for some team members.
  • Risk: the security review for the notification API may not finish this week, which would delay the UI story. Mitigation: Tom will request a review slot today.
  • Risk: the analytics event spec is still a draft. Mitigation: Marcus and Aisha will agree on a minimal event set by Wednesday.
  • Risk: only one QA engineer is available. Mitigation: developers will write automated tests for their own stories.

5. Wrap-up

  • Priya recapped the commitments and action items, and the team confirmed the sprint scope.
  • Sprint review is scheduled for Dec 7 at 2:00 PM.

Decisions

D1. The Sprint 24 goal is to ship the redesigned onboarding flow to 25% of new users and complete notification preferences.
D2. The sprint is committed at 38 story points, including a 4-point bug and regression buffer.
D3. The onboarding UI story stays as one 8-point story and will not be split.
D4. The in-app tooltip tour is deferred to the backlog until it is refined and re-estimated.
D5. Only one tech debt item, the database client upgrade, is included this sprint.
D6. From the next sprint on, design hand-offs must be complete before sprint planning.
